In mathematics, the '''Cartan–Hadamard conjecture''' is a fundamental problem in [[Riemannian geometry]] and [[geometric measure theory]] which states that the classical [[isoperimetric inequality]] may be generalized to spaces of nonpositive [[sectional curvature]], known as [[Hadamard manifold|Cartan–Hadamard manifolds]]. The conjecture, which  is named after French mathematicians [[Élie Cartan]] and [[Jacques Hadamard]], may be traced back to work of [[André Weil]] in 1926.

== History ==
The conjecture, in all dimensions, was first stated explicitly in 1976  by [[Thierry Aubin]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Aubin|first=Thierry|date=1976|title=Problèmes isopérimétriques et espaces de Sobolev|journal=Journal of Differential Geometry|volume=11|issue=4|pages=573–598|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214433725|issn=0022-040X|doi-access=free |bibcode=1976JDGeo..1133725A }}</ref> and a few years later by [[Mikhail Leonidovich Gromov|Misha Gromov]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Metric structures for Riemannian and non-Riemannian spaces|last=Gromov | first=Mikhael|date=1999|publisher=Birkhäuser|isbn=0817638989|oclc=37201427}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TxN0QgAACAAJ|title=Structures métriques pour les variétés riemanniennes|last=Gromov|first=Mikhael|date=1981|publisher=CEDIC/Fernand Nathan|isbn=9782712407148|language=fr}}</ref>  [[Yuri Burago]] and 
[[Viktor Zalgaller]].<ref>{{Cite book|title=Geometricheskie neravenstva|last1=Burago|first1=Yuri|last2=Zalgaller|first2=Viktor|date=1980|publisher="Nauka, " Leningradskoe otd-nie|oclc=610467367}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last1=Burago|first1=Yuri|last2=Zalgaller|first2=Viktor|date=1988|title=Geometric Inequalities|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-07441-1|isbn=978-3-642-05724-3}}</ref> In dimension 2 this fact had already been established in 1926 by [[André Weil]]<ref>{{Citation|last1=Weil|first1=M. André|chapter=Sur les surfaces à courbure négative|date=1979|title=Œuvres Scientifiques Collected Papers|pages=1–2|publisher=Springer New York|isbn=9781475717068|last2=Hadamard|first2=M.|doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-1705-1_1|doi-broken-date=1 July 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Weil  |first= André |date=3 May 1926 | others=Presentée par Jacques Hadamard |title=Sur les surfaces à courbure négative |journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences de Paris |volume=182 |issue=Seance du 3 Mai 1926 |publisher=Gauthier-Villars Paris | url=https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k31356|pages=1069–1071 }}</ref> and rediscovered in 1933 by [[Edwin F. Beckenbach|Beckenbach]] and [[Tibor Radó|Rado]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Beckenbach|first1=E. F.|last2=Rado|first2=T.|date=1933|title=Subharmonic Functions and Surfaces of Negative Curvature|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|volume=35|issue=3|pages=662|doi=10.2307/1989854|issn=0002-9947|jstor=1989854|doi-access=free}}</ref> 

According to [[Marcel Berger]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=A Panoramic View of Riemannian Geometry|last=Berger, Marcel.|date=2013|publisher=Springer Berlin|isbn=978-3-642-62121-5|oclc=864568506}}</ref> Weil, who was a student of Hadamard at the time, was prompted to work on this problem due to "a question asked during or after a Hadamard seminar at the [[Collège de France]]" by the probability theorist [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]].

In dimensions 3 and 4 the conjecture was proved by [[Bruce Kleiner]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kleiner |first=Bruce |date=1992 |title=An isoperimetric comparison theorem |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |volume=108 |issue=1 |pages=37–47 |doi=10.1007/bf02100598 |issn=0020-9910 |bibcode=1992InMat.108...37K |s2cid=16836013}}</ref> in 1992, and [[Chris Croke]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Croke|first=Christopher B.|date=1984|title=A sharp four dimensional isoperimetric inequality|journal=[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]]|volume=59|issue=1|pages=187–192|doi=10.1007/bf02566344|s2cid=120138158|issn=0010-2571}}</ref> in 1984 respectively. In 2026, Shibing Chen, [[Mohammad Ghomi]], and Peng Wang posted a proof of the conjecture in dimension 5.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Chen |first1=Shibing |title=The Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in dimension five |date=2026-09-10 |eprint=2609.11005 |last2=Ghomi |first2=Mohammad |last3=Wang |first3=Peng |class=math.DG }}</ref> In a subsequent paper they showed that their approach establishes the conjecture in dimensions up to at least 9.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Chen |first1=Shibing |title=The isoperimetric inequality and CMC hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds |date=2026-09-17 |eprint=2609.20517 |last2=Ghomi |first2=Mohammad |last3=Wang |first3=Peng |class=math.DG }}</ref>

Weil's proof relies on [[conformal map]]s and [[harmonic analysis]], Croke's proof is based on an inequality of [[Luis Santaló|Santaló]] in [[integral geometry]], while Kleiner adopts a [[Calculus of variations|variational approach]] which reduces the problem to an estimate for [[total curvature]]. [[Mohammad Ghomi]] and [[Joel Spruck]] have shown that Kleiner's approach will work in all dimensions where the total curvature inequality holds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ghomi|first1=Mohammad|last2=Spruck|first2=Joel|date=2022-01-04|title=Total Curvature and the Isoperimetric Inequality in Cartan–Hadamard Manifolds|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s12220-021-00801-2|journal=The Journal of Geometric Analysis|language=en|volume=32|issue=2|pages=50|doi=10.1007/s12220-021-00801-2|issn=1559-002X|arxiv=1908.09814|s2cid=255558870 }}</ref> The proof of Chen-Ghomi-Wang is based on a sharp estimate for the area of [[Constant-mean-curvature surface|constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces]] which gives a unified proof of the conjecture in all dimensions from 3 to 9.

In 2026 [[Mohammad Ghomi]] and John Stavroulakis proved the local version of the conjecture by showing that if the metric of the Euclidean ball is perturbed to one with nonpositive curvature then the Isoperimetric ratio will go up.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ghomi |first1=Mohammad |last2=Ioannis Stavroulakis |first2=John |date=2026 |title=A Local Isoperimetric Inequality for Balls with Nonpositive Curvature |url=https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnag043 |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |volume=2026 |issue=6 |article-number=rnag043 |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnag043 |issn=1073-7928|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Generalized form ==
The conjecture has a more general form, sometimes called the "generalized Cartan–Hadamard conjecture"<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kloeckner|first1=Benoît|last2=Kuperberg|first2=Greg|date=2019-07-08|title=The Cartan–Hadamard conjecture and the Little Prince|journal=Revista Matemática Iberoamericana|volume=35|issue=4|pages=1195–1258|doi=10.4171/rmi/1082|issn=0213-2230|arxiv=1303.3115|s2cid=119165853}}</ref> which states that if the curvature of the ambient Cartan–Hadamard manifold M is bounded  above by a nonpositive constant k, then the least perimeter enclosures in M, for any given volume, cannot have smaller perimeter than a sphere enclosing the same volume 
in the model space of constant curvature k.

The generalized conjecture has been established only in dimension 2 by [[Gerrit Bol]],<ref>{{Cite book|title=Isoperimetrische Ungleichungen für Bereiche auf Flächen.|last=Bol, G.|oclc=946388942}}</ref> and dimension 3 by Kleiner.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kleiner|first=Bruce|date=1992|title=An isoperimetric comparison theorem|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=108|issue=1|pages=37–47|doi=10.1007/bf02100598|issn=0020-9910|bibcode=1992InMat.108...37K|s2cid=16836013}}</ref>

==Applications==
Immediate applications of the conjecture include  extensions of the [[Sobolev inequality]] and [[Rayleigh–Faber–Krahn inequality]] to spaces of nonpositive curvature.
